sources.entry: micro - A terminal-based text editor that aims to be easy to use and intuitive, while also taking advantage of the capabilities of modern terminals.

summary.one_liner: micro is a terminal-based text editor meant to be easy to use and intuitive, shipped as a single static binary with no dependencies and positioned as a successor to nano.
summary.what_it_does: micro is a terminal text editor that runs over SSH or locally and is distributed as a single, statically linked binary. It offers common keybindings (Ctrl-s, Ctrl-c, Ctrl-v, Ctrl-z) that can be rebound, multiple cursors, splits and tabs, and a nano-style menu for remembering keybindings. Mouse support includes drag-to-select, double-click for word selection, and triple-click for line selection. Other built-in features include syntax highlighting for over 130 languages, a diff gutter, simple autocompletion, persistent undo, linting notifications, macros, and a plugin system written in Lua with a built-in plugin manager. It also reads buffers from stdin and uses the system clipboard when the appropriate tools are available.
use_cases: quick config file editing on a server
editing source code in a terminal
piping command output into an editor
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL>; cd micro; make build
stack: Go (1.19 or greater to build from source)
notable: Single static binary with no dependencies; CGO_ENABLED=1 gives a dynamically linked build instead
Built-in plugin manager that installs, removes, and updates Lua plugins
Nano-like help menu and built-in help system accessed with Ctrl-e
Extensive mouse support including word and line selection
caveats: Windows is supported but Mingw and Cygwin are not officially supported (winpty workaround may work); Plan9 and NaCl are not supported
On macOS, keybindings use Ctrl or Alt rather than Cmd, and terminal configuration is needed so Alt/Option events are forwarded
Clipboard integration on Linux requires xclip, xsel, or wl-clipboard; otherwise an internal clipboard is used
Terminals with limited color support (including many Windows consoles) need the simple color scheme
